title: Independent takeoff and received return
effort: Express force through one takeoff leg and one returning arm while keeping reception controlled.
brief: Open with Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception as the controlled lower-body force anchor. Express force through one takeoff leg and one returning arm while keeping reception controlled.

entries.name: Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
entries.sourceName: Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception
entries.instruction: Main independent stance-leg upward push with a deliberately broader receiving base. Stand on one leg, make a small controlled dip and project a modest height; bring both feet under the pelvis and receive on two feet, holding 2 s. Three attempts per takeoff leg. No extra preparatory hop. Recovery: complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section Use instead: two bouts of three bilateral settled-start squat jumps with hands at hips, 10 s between reps and 60 s between bouts, then the same 90 s transition; hold the start 2 s without a second dip and receive on both feet for 2 s. This replaces unilateral takeoffs with bilateral takeoffs and differs from E3 grounded single-leg force. If bilateral receiving also fails, stop the remaining flight work and record a modified session. This replaces remaining work in this slot; follow an explicit replacement dose if stated, otherwise keep the remaining dose/rest. Log changed events or laterality.

explosive_progression_note: Single-Leg Vertical Takeoff — two-foot floor reception changes vertical projection to one-leg takeoff while retaining two-foot reception. Medicine Ball Two-Hand Receive to Single-Arm Forward Return links a two-hand feed to one-arm return, and Externally supplied rotational scoop return adds a secure handoff before rotation; its handoffs are supplies, not airborne catches. This post-consolidation prescription introduces these constraints without evidence that the athlete has earned them. Compared with Class 18, prescribed ball releases change from 4 to 10, bilateral foot-landing events change from 2 to 6, airborne feed catches change from 0 to 6, secure handoffs change from 0 to 4, explosive set/side bouts change from 10 to 12. Review actual recovery and qualify each support and receiving task separately: level takeoff, controlled two-foot reception, secure single-arm ball control and feeder clearance before turning. Use the listed bilateral settled-start jumps for remaining E1 attempts when single-leg takeoff is unqualified; use self-started single-arm throws for remaining E2 attempts and self-held paused scoops for remaining E6 attempts when their receiving arrangements fail. Record changed takeoffs, catches and handoffs; do not add retries.
